headline: Sensex and Nifty decline as rising crude oil prices, IT weakness, and FPI outflows weigh on sentiment.

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Rising crude oil prices dragged market sentiment.
Selling pressure in IT and bank stocks weighed on benchmark indices.
Continued foreign portfolio investor (FPI) outflows contributed to the decline.
Investor caution ahead of the US Federal Reserve's interest rate decision.
whatHappening: Sensex fell 353 points as Nifty dropped below the 22,700 mark.
City Union Bank posted a 26% jump in Q2 net profit to ₹416 crore.
GAIL India announced a $63 million investment in a heating unit at its Ratnagiri LNG terminal.
Dr. Reddy's Laboratories received a VAI tag from the US FDA for its Srikakulam facility, closing the inspection.
summary: Indian benchmark indices closed lower today due to weakness in IT and banking stocks alongside rising crude oil prices. Foreign portfolio outflows and caution ahead of the US Fed decision further impacted market sentiment. On the corporate front, City Union Bank, GAIL India, and Dr. Reddy's posted encouraging updates.
